review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] declarations and no simp-set attributes, and no rewrite cycle is credible. The main simp-interface issues are in the hand-built isomorphisms, which have no simp lemmas for their components. The naturality lemmas are correctly not simp. I checked Mathlib's `AddEquiv.toAddCommGrpIso`, which is `@[simps]`-generated through `to_additive`, and `HomologicalComplex.homologyMapIso`, which is `@[simps]`. I did not run Lean, so I have not checked that the replacements compile or that the `rfl`/`simp` steps still go through. I did not look at downstream uses outside this file.

findings.problem: The isomorphism is assembled field by field, with `hom`, `inv` and two hand-written `ext x; exact ...symm_apply_apply` proofs. This repeats what Mathlib's `AddEquiv.toAddCommGrpIso` already provides, and that definition is `@[simps]`-generated, so it has simp lemmas for `hom` and `inv`. Because the bespoke `Iso` has no such lemmas, nothing in the file lets `simp` or `dsimp` reduce `.hom`/`.inv` to `ofHom (equiv.toAddMonoidHom)` and then to `equiv x`. The same file already uses `.toAddCommGrpIso` in `cohomologySourceCoyonedaIsoSections` and in `HPrimeEquivRestrictedResolutionSectionsHomology`, so the style is inconsistent.
findings.proposed_change: Define the isomorphism as `(AddCommGrpCat.… extPositiveIsoHomology q hq).toAddCommGrpIso`, applied to the `AddEquiv`, and drop the manual `hom`/`inv`/`hom_inv_id`/`inv_hom_id` fields. The result is then definitionally the same data with Mathlib's `toAddCommGrpIso_hom`/`toAddCommGrpIso_inv` simp lemmas available. If the type needs adjusting to match the declared `H' G q U`, state the target through the same equivalence.
findings.benefit: Readers and downstream proofs get canonical simp lemmas for the component maps. This avoids unfolding with `dsimp [HPrimeIsoGlobalResolutionHomComplexHomology]`, as the naturality lemmas do, and removes about 20 lines of duplicated boilerplate.

findings.problem: This is the same pattern as `HPrimeIsoGlobalResolutionHomComplexHomology`. The `AddEquiv`-to-`AddCommGrpCat`-iso conversion is written out manually instead of through the `@[simps]`-generated `toAddCommGrpIso`. As a result no `hom`/`inv` simp lemmas exist for this iso, and `restrictedAcyclicResolution_extPositiveIsoHomology_hom_naturality` has to start from `ext x` and a direct appeal to `extPositiveIsoHomology_naturality`.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the body with `(… extPositiveIsoHomology q hq).toAddCommGrpIso`. The theorem statements that mention `.hom` then continue to work. The naturality proof can use the generated `toAddCommGrpIso_hom` simp lemma before `ext`.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical normal form for the iso components, the proof boilerplate is shorter, and the two ext-positive isomorphisms in the file are built in the same way.

findings.problem: Six lemmas (lines 309, 692, 905, 1073, 1234 and the pattern around them) turn a `homologyMapIso` naturality square into a `homologyMap` square by unfolding the definition with `dsimp [HomologicalComplex.homologyMapIso]`. They then run `rw [← homologyMap_comp, <chain-level naturality>, homologyMap_comp]`. Mathlib marks `HomologicalComplex.homologyMapIso` as `@[simps]`, so its `hom` and `inv` simp lemmas are the intended interface. Unfolding the definition bypasses that interface and exposes the internal structure of the iso. The same chain-level-to-homology argument is repeated five times with no reusable lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Use the generated `HomologicalComplex.homologyMapIso_hom` simp lemma in place of unfolding the definition. Better, factor out a single general lemma of the form `homologyMap φ q ≫ (homologyMapIso e' q).hom = (homologyMapIso e q).hom ≫ homologyMap ψ q` from `φ ≫ e'.hom = e.hom ≫ ψ`, as a `@[reassoc]` statement, and instantiate it at each site. The existing `Functor.map` lemmas `HomologicalComplex.homologyMap_comp` and `homologyMapIso_hom` would then be rewritten once rather than re-proved at five call sites.
findings.benefit: The proofs stop depending on how `homologyMapIso` is defined internally. The repeated rewrite sequences in five lemmas become short one-line applications.
